“‘Ma’am, gold toh personal jewellery thi… Capital Gain kaise ho gaya?’' 😭


Just because your gold jewellery was personally used, it doesn't mean its sale is automatically tax-free.



Gold jewellery is treated as a Capital Asset under the Income-tax Act.


So, when you sell it, you may have Capital Gains.


Selling Price – Cost of Acquisition = Capital Gain(subject to applicable adjustments/rules)

• If Held for > 24 months, then it's Long Term 

•If Held for 24 months or less, then it's Short term


For transfers on or after 23 July 2024, LTCG on such assets is generally taxed at 12.5% without indexation


And if the jewellery was acquired through gift/inheritance, different rules can apply for determining the cost and holding period.



💀Disclaimer -

“Gold ki purity check karne se pehle, tax treatment check kar lo”
